Use case: scientific-educational. A simplified educational illustration of a human embryo at EIGHT completed gestational weeks. Crucial early anatomy: curved C-shaped body, very large rounded head bent forward, small dark eye area, elongated short arms ending in PADDLE SHAPED HANDS WITHOUT SEPARATE FINGERS, short developing legs without developed feet or toes. No mature baby face, no hair, no newborn body. Clean black contour lines and warm peach/orange flat fills, minimal shadows, gentle non-graphic educational style. Full subject centered on white square background. No text, labels, border or other objects. A small curved cord may extend from abdomen.

Use case: scientific-educational. Create a NEW square, simplified prenatal developmental illustration. Subject: A small prenatal fetus around twelve completed gestational weeks, large head relative to body, delicate slender arms and bent legs, tiny distinct fingers, closed eyelids, relaxed curved profile. Optional short softly curved umbilical cord; no uterus, placenta, blood or exposed internal structures. Preserve early developmental proportions: this is NOT a newborn. For week 6/8 use early embryonic anatomy with a curved C-shaped body, tiny immature limb buds or paddles, NO fully formed baby face, NO fingers or toes, NO chubby mature baby. For week 20 use a slender fetal torso and thin limbs, NO chubby cheeks or baby fat. Pure clean white background, full body centered, no frame, no text, no labels, no watermark, no scale bars. Non-graphic and gentle. Style: Clean strong black outlines, limited flat warm peach and orange fills, contemporary friendly drawn illustration, no gradients.
